'''Irene Mulvey''' is an American [[mathematician]] and progressive activist.

== Career ==
Mulvey completed her doctoral dissertation, titled ''Periodic, Recurrent and Non-Wandering Points for Continuous Maps of the Circle'' at [[Wesleyan University]] in 1982, where she was advised by Ethan Coven.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|38894}}</ref> She was appointed to a professorship at [[Fairfield University]] in 1985.<ref>{{cite news |title=Fairfield Professor Irene Mulvey, PhD, Elected AAUP President |url=https://www.fairfield.edu/news/archive/2020/august/irene-mulvey-elected-aaup-president.html |accessdate=October 12, 2020 |publisher=Fairfield University |date=August 2020}}</ref>

=== President of the American Association of University Professors ===
In July 2020, Mulvey was elected president of the [[American Association of University Professors]], succeeding [[Rudy Fichtenbaum]], serving in that role until June 2024.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Flaherty |first1=Colleen |title=AAUP Announces Election Results |url=https://www.insidehighered.com/quicktakes/2020/07/22/aaup-announces-election-results |accessdate=October 12, 2020 |work=Inside Higher Ed |date=July 22, 2020}}</ref> During her tenure as AAUP President, she claimed that state bills targeted at [[diversity, equity and inclusion]] programs damage not only higher education but also democracy.<ref>{{cite news|last=Cineas|first1=Fabiola|title=The right-wing assault on higher education|url=https://www.vox.com/policy/23762357/republican-attack-higher-education|website=Vox|date=Jun 17, 2023|access-date=Jun 19, 2023}}</ref>
